served: gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards)
needle EMG (continuous motor unit activity at rest)
results: 1. walking backward: the slow, guarded, wide-based pattern PERSISTS
2. running: cannot run; the pattern does not normalise
3. gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards): no change - the gait is not distractible
4. muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): genuine axial and lower-limb rigidity on passive movement
5. trial of benzodiazepine (diazepam): clear improvement in stiffness and in the gait
6. anti-GAD65 antibodies: MARKEDLY ELEVATED (high-titre, typically >2000 U/mL) - diagnostic in this clinical context
7. needle EMG (continuous motor unit activity at rest): CONTINUOUS motor unit activity at rest in agonist and antagonist simultaneously, abolished by diazepam
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Stiff Person Syndrome — autoimmune, associated with high-titre anti-GAD65 antibodies (reduced central GABAergic inhibition producing axial and lower-limb rigidity with continuous motor unit activity that is benzodiazepine-responsive).

Alternatives:
1. Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM) — a related GAD65-spectrum disorder
2. Autoimmune stiff-limb syndrome — focal lower-limb variant of SPS
3. Paraneoplastic stiff person spectrum disorder (e.g., anti-amphiphysin) — though the markedly elevated anti-GAD65 makes this less likely
dx: Stiff Person Syndrome — autoimmune, associated with high-titre anti-GAD65 antibodies (reduced central GABAergic inhibition producing axial and lower-limb rigidity with continuous motor unit activity that is benzodiazepine-responsive).
